clue.text: Chat show's opening minute promising much — but will never deliver

indicators.note: opening means only the first letter of the word show is wanted

parts.note: S is the first letter of show's

parts.words: promising much — but will never deliver
parts.note: someone who is all talk makes big promises and never follows through

explanation.surface: A sceptic's view of a chat show: the opening minute promises plenty and the programme never delivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Small talk is light, polite conversation about unimportant matters, a synonym for idle chat.

clue.text: Clue suggesting Rich CEO of The Range is too large?

indicators.note: Clue suggesting says the clue words are what the answer produces when read as an instruction

parts.note: spoilt read as an anagram signal turns the letters of for choice into rich ceo of

explanation.surface: A clue about the wealthy boss of The Range, a British homeware store chain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, the answer says 'for choice' is spoilt (rearranged), giving the clue's Rich CEO of: the answer is the clue that would produce those words. The Range is a UK home and garden retailer, but range here means selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Being spoilt for choice idiomatically means having so many options that choosing is hard, an overly large selection.

clue.text: Call secretary about old primate

indicators.note: about means the combined pieces are turned round

parts.note: to name is to call
PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: A secretary is asked to telephone about an old monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An apeman is a primitive hominid, an early ancestor of humans halfway between ape and man.

clue.text: City's unusually long leases

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of long leases are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A city is known for its unusually long property leases.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Angeles is the largest city in California, home of Hollywood.

clue.text: Somehow R2D2 showed up

indicators.note: somehow means the pieces are jumbled into some new order

parts.note: each 2 in the droid's name stands for the answer to 2 down, the primate, so the letters are R, that answer, D and that answer again

explanation.surface: The Star Wars droid R2D2 somehow turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: Each 2 in the droid's name is a cross-reference to 2 down, APE, so the fodder is R, APE, D, APE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have appeared is to have arrived or come into view, a synonym for showed up.

clue.text: Quiet son becoming king — one should let off steam

indicators.note: becoming means the letter for son turns into the letter for king

parts.note: to settle is to quieten or calm
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A quiet son becomes king and needs to let off steam.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettle boils water and releases steam from its spout, so it lets off steam literally rather than figuratively.

clue.text: Teachers' cane

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the teaching ... of a school, used here like a possessive noun
second meaning: a walking stick or rod

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the cane once wielded by schoolteachers; the two words are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's employees are its staff, and a staff is also a long stick carried for walking or support.

clue.text: Hide second family

parts.note: kin are family

explanation.surface: Someone hides a second family from the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb about concealing the family; it is the noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is the skin of an animal, the two nouns being synonyms.

clue.text: Hugely enjoying a party circuit

parts.note: a do is a party
a ring is a circular course or circuit

explanation.surface: Someone is hugely enjoying a round of parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring means loving or delighting in something intensely, close to enjoying it hugely.

clue.text: Go mad using only characters onboard ship — shall then do Fyffes bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange
only characters onboard ship means the letters within S and S (steamship) at the ends are used

parts.note: Fyffes is a banana importer; dropping the outer S letters leaves the fodder

explanation.surface: Fyffes, a fruit company, ships its bananas, and somebody on board goes mad.
explanation.walkthrough: SS is a steamship, so the letters on board are those between the outer S letters of 'shall then do Fyffes': HALLTHENDOFYFFE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly off the handle is an idiom for losing one's temper suddenly and wildly.

clue.text: No hiding space over introduction to star signs

indicators.note: over in a down-style reading means the letters are turned back to front
hiding means the word No conceals the space inside it

parts.note: taken as written
an em is a printer's unit of space

indicators.note: introduction to means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: S is the first letter of star

explanation.surface: An astrologer refuses to keep space hidden from a beginner's guide to star signs.
explanation.walkthrough: An em is a printer's unit of space, the width of the letter M, a convention worth knowing in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Omens are portents or signs of what is to come, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cut working wage to cover father's gift

indicators.note: to cover means the word for wage wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: pay is a wage
to trim is to cut
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: An employer trims a working wage to pay for a gift from father.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrimony is property inherited from one's father, literally a paternal legacy or bequest.

clue.text: Sad sheriffs suggest releasing Western

indicators.note: releasing means letting the letter for Western go free from the word for sheriffs

parts.note: sheriffs are lawmen
to table a motion is to suggest it for discussion

explanation.surface: Sad sheriffs propose letting a Western film go free.
explanation.walkthrough: To table, in British usage, is to put forward for discussion, not to shelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamentable means deplorable or regrettable, a synonym for sad in the sense of pitiful.

clue.text: See 2
Turning heads in fifth form, including teacher's pet

indicators.note: turning means the collected letters are read in reverse
heads in means the first letters of each of the following words

parts.note: F is the first letter of fifth
F is the first letter of form
I is the first letter of including
T is the first letter of teacher's

explanation.surface: Pupils in the fifth form turn heads by sheltering the teacher's favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teacher's pet' reads as a phrase, but pet stands alone as the definition and teacher's gives a letter. The heads F, F, I, T are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet is a fit of sulking or bad temper, and a tiff is a petty quarrel or huff.

clue.text: C3PO satisfied TV show's gauge of audience approval

parts.note: the droid's name gives C and PO, and the 3 between them stands for the answer to 3 down, abbreviated LA
met means satisfied, as a demand met
ER is an American hospital drama on TV

explanation.surface: The Star Wars droid C3PO is pleased with a TV show's measure of applause.
explanation.walkthrough: The 3 in the droid's name is a cross-reference: 3 down is LOS ANGELES, abbreviated LA.
explanation.definitionFit: A clapometer is a device on TV talent shows that measures the volume of applause.

clue.text: See 16
Inclined to appropriate action — hung around with Spooner's relation

indicators.note: Spooner's relation is the version told by Dr Spooner, who swapped the first sounds of words

parts.note: a fight is military action
lingered means hung around

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to take appropriate action hangs around with a relative of Spooner.
explanation.definitionFit: A light-fingered person is prone to stealing, and to appropriate something is to take it without permission.

clue.text: Partially backing bonsai pot business — it gives urban sorts a taste of country life

definitions.text: it gives urban sorts a taste of country life

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
Partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bonsai pot business partly backed by city dwellers wanting a taste of the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtopia is suburbia seen as sprawl, offering town dwellers a semi-rural setting.

clue.text: Increase level for audience

indicators.note: for audience means the word is heard by listeners rather than read

parts.note: to raze a building is to level it to the ground

explanation.surface: A sound engineer increases the level for the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A raise is an increase, especially in pay, and to raise something is to lift it higher.

clue.text: Found swapping Sierra and parking — I'm on drive

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: swapping means the letters for Sierra and parking trade places

parts.note: to found a business is to set it up

explanation.surface: Found by swapping Sierra for a parking space, says someone on a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: S is Sierra in the NATO alphabet and P is parking; swapping them in SETUP gives PETUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or drive that moves something forward.

clue.text: Copper succeeded stopping break out — turning back one who's 16/15

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: stopping means the letter for succeeded plugs a gap in the other word
turning back means the word for break out is read in reverse

parts.note: to erupt is to break out
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A policeman, having succeeded in stopping a jailbreak, turns back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' makes TPURE from ERUPT, and 'stopping' puts S inside it. The definition points to 16/15, which is LIGHT-FINGERED.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutpurse is an old word for a pickpocket, a thief who once cut purses from belts.

clue.text: Wine spot creates problem for photo

parts.note: red is a type of wine
to spot is to eye or notice

explanation.surface: A wine spot on a photograph creates a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-eye is the reddened pupils caused by camera flash, a common flaw in photographs.

clue.text: Endless trouble accommodating 100 beds

indicators.note: accommodating means the shortened trouble word holds the hundred
endless means the trouble word loses its last letter

parts.note: fuss is trouble or bother
a ton is a hundred

explanation.surface: Endless trouble housing a hundred beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Futons are Japanese-style mattresses that serve as beds or sofas.

clue.text: Occasionally they upset build up

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of the following words is used

parts.note: the alternate letters taken are the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: People who are upset sometimes build things up out of proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: To hype something is to promote or publicise it extravagantly, to talk it up.

clue.text: Short Disney film about period princess using sound and vision?

indicators.note: about means the shortened film title goes around the other pieces
short means the film's title loses its last letter

parts.note: Mulan is a Disney animated film
a period is a stretch of time
Di is Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A short Disney film about a princess from a historical period.
explanation.walkthrough: Mulan is Disney's 1998 animated film about a Chinese heroine; Di is the usual crossword shorthand for Princess Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: Multimedia presentations combine several forms such as audio, video and text, so they use sound and vision together.

clue.text: Terribly discontented, vandalise railway

indicators.note: discontented means the word vandalise loses its contents, leaving only the ends

parts.note: V and E are the outer letters of vandalise

explanation.surface: Terribly unhappy people vandalise a railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' looks like an anagram signal but it is the definition, very.
explanation.definitionFit: Very and terribly are both intensifying adverbs, as in terribly sorry.

clue.text: Informed where to go quietly

parts.note: in the loo is where one goes to the toilet; loo is British slang for a toilet
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone is told where they can go to the toilet discreetly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the loop is an idiom for being kept up to date and aware of what is happening.

clue.text: Tramp making a name for fashion

indicators.note: making, paired with for, means one letter is replaced by another
for marks the swap: the name letter stands in place of a

parts.note: to tread is to tramp

explanation.surface: A homeless tramp becomes a fashion name.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a current fashion or general direction of taste.

clue.text: See 21
South Africa's starters told to get try

indicators.note: told means the letters are spoken aloud, their names sounding out the answer

parts.note: the starting letters of South and Africa's are S and A, which spoken are ess and ay

explanation.surface: South Africa's starting players are told to go and score a try in rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the letters S and A are 'ess' and 'ay'.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt, so to essay something is to try it.

clue.text: Something used to fence around base — estate's boundaries handling variable wind offshore

indicators.note: around means the fencing weapon wraps around the letter for base

parts.note: a sabre is one of the three weapons used in fencing
e is the base of natural logarithms

indicators.note: handling means the boundary letters hold the variable between them

parts.note: the boundaries of estate are its first and last letters, E and E
z is a common algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A fence around the base of an estate copes with a changeable offshore wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea breeze is a light wind blowing from the sea towards land, but here offshore means at sea.
